subject: DPA exhibit — residency, retention & erase procedure: clarifying Q&A and redline
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Operations <legal.ops@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Exhibit questions — residency / erase timeline

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks for sending over the DPA exhibit. Legal Ops had a couple of targeted questions so we don’t have to redline blind. High-level asks: 

- Section 3(b) requests "full deletion within 30 days of termination". Can you confirm whether that 30 day clock applies to backups and cross-region replicas, or only the primary datastore?
- We need a simple certification procedure: we must receive a certificate of deletion with a chain-of-evidence describing what was wiped and when. Can you provide a template or confirm Redwood can supply a stamped certificate?
- For data residency: our security team would prefer that customer data for Acme be kept in the us-east-1 region unless a request to replicate is explicitly authorized. Is there an operational mechanism to pin region for the account and enforce no automatic cross-region snapshots?

We attached the exhibit with our in-line comments. Would like to resolve non-technical language quickly; we can handle operations details after that.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jenkins
Senior Counsel, Data Protection
Acme Cloud
attachments: DPA_Exhibit-Residency-Retention_v1.1.docx (docx, 124KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit questions — residency / erase timeline

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Responding inline and with a suggested redline summary below.

1) 30-day deletion clock: The 30-day timeline in Section 3(b) as written is Redwood's commit to remove customer-accessible production data artifacts. Practically, full propagation through backups/replicas can stretch beyond that window depending on replication topology. To make this explicit we propose: 
  - Redline language: "Redwood will delete production data and render it inaccessible within 30 days of termination; backups and secondary replicas will be scheduled for deletion and final wipe no later than 60 days from termination unless otherwise required by law or agreed operational hold."
  - Rationale: this preserves your requirement for prompt deletion while giving Redwood a bounded operational window to perform safe wipe/restore-blocking procedures across snapshots and long-tail replicas.

2) Certificate of deletion: Redwood can provide a deletion certificate. Proposed scope: account identifier, dataset identifiers (logical), deletion actions taken (primary delete, snapshot tombstone, backup overwrite/retirement), timestamped ops runbook reference and an SRE ticket identifier. We can use the attached Erase_Playbook_Summary.pdf as the operational appendix.

3) Residency / pinning: We support region pinning at the account level. Operational note: we require an initial account-level residency selection (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). Automatic cross-region replication is disabled by default for customer data; managed replication (for DR) requires explicit opt-in and a signed change request. We'll add explicit language to the exhibit.

I attached a short proposed redline snippet in the doc and an ops summary for deletion certification. If that looks OK from Legal, we can surface the technical SRE steps for evidence collection.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: Erase_Playbook_Summary.pdf (pdf, 56KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: operational implications of 30/60 day split

Irene / Laura — quick ops check from my side:

Summary of proposed ask: production data inaccessible by 30 days, backups/final wipe by 60 days.

Operational impacts and suggestions:
- Snapshot retention policies: many customers run daily snapshots with a 90 day retention default. If we move to a 60 day forced final wipe we need a decommission job that forces immediate tombstone + overwrite scheduling for any snapshot chain linked to Acme account. That job needs SRE review (OPS-7423).
- For the deletion certificate: SRE can produce a machine-generated manifest and a signed verification from KMS indicating keys rotated/zeroed where applicable. We should avoid long textual narratives—Legal usually wants a structured manifest + signed attestation.
- Edge case: archived logs stored for observability (not customer-content) may include event traces referencing tenant IDs; we can redact or truncate but need to call this out in the exhibit as "operational logs excluded" with retention bounds.

Ask: Can Legal accept 60 days for final backup wipe, and accept a structured deletion manifest rather than a prose certificate? If yes, Ben will draft the manifest template.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer (Onboarding) — Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Operations <legal.ops@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit questions — residency / erase timeline

Irene / Ben — thanks for the rapid responses and practical framing. Legal is comfortable with the 30/60 split provided we get two items: 

1) A one-page deletion certificate (PDF) with the structured manifest fields Ben mentioned (account id, dataset ids, snapshot ids, timestamps, SRE ticket id, KMS attestation id). The template can be machine-generated.
2) Explicit text in the exhibit that "Automatic cross-region replication is disabled unless customer explicitly opts in by signed change request" (we will accept this operational control).

We will mark the exhibit as "accepted subject to incorporation of the two items above" and circulate redline comments after lunch. Can you please: 
- Share a sample manifest template by EOD Pacific? 
- Add the cross-region sentence into the exhibit doc and re-send?

If you can do both, Legal will stop additional back-and-forth and we’ll proceed to final DPA signature.

Sara
Sara Jenkins
Senior Counsel, Data Protection
Acme Cloud
